note: Literature directly supports that biallelic RNU2-2 variants lead to transcript instability and loss of expression, mechanistically distinguishing them from dominant disorders.

evidence.text: Whole-blood RNA sequencing showed a >90% reduction in expression of pathogenic U2-2 alleles in biallelic cases and carriers, pointing to a loss-of-expression mechanism for recessive RNU2-2 syndrome.

source.title: Biallelic variants in RNU2-2 cause the most prevalent known recessive neurodevelopmental disorder
source.quote: Whole-blood RNA sequencing data showed a >90% reduction in the expression of pathogenic U2-2 alleles in biallelic cases and monoallelic carriers, albeit with wild-type compensation in carriers, pointing to a loss-of-expression mechanism.

numbers.metric: reduction in expression of pathogenic U2-2 alleles

evidence.text: Biallelic RNU2-2 variants correlate with reduced U2-2 abundance and an altered U2-2 to U2-1 ratio, showing that the recessive disorder is mechanistically distinct from the dominant disorder.

source.title: Biallelic variants in RNU2-2 cause a remarkably frequent developmental and epileptic encephalopathy
source.quote: We find that candidate biallelic variants are significantly correlated with reduced U2-2 abundance, implicating compromised transcript stability as a probable pathomechanism. We identify a decreased ratio of U2-2 to its paralog U2-1 as a potential diagnostic biomarker for this condition. We show that the recessive RNU2-2 syndrome is genetically, clinically and mechanistically distinct from the dominant RNU2-2 disorder.
